title: Late Pleistocene megafaunal extinction in the Americas
summary: During the terminal Pleistocene, more than thirty-five genera of large mammals vanished from North America and over fifty from South America, including mammoths, mastodons, ground sloths, saber-toothed cats, and dire wolves. High-precision dating demonstrates a concentrated extinction window between roughly 13,800 and 11,400 calibrated years ago, culminating around 12,900 years ago. This catastrophic biotic turnover permanently transformed Western Hemisphere ecosystems and was driven by interacting pressures from abrupt climate warming, fire-driven vegetation shifts, and human hunting.
